newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Britain's Labour plans tough rail rules.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Britain's Labour plans tough rail rules.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has promised a regulatory clampdown on the rail industry if it wins the next election, citing franchise operators and Railtrack Plc as the most likely targets.

Andrew Smith, Labour's shadow transport secretary, said he would use the maximum existing regulatory powers and might even consider tougher rules to force Railtrack, operator of the British rail network, to meet its investment obligations.
Labour is tipped to win the next election, due by May 22, as it rides high in opinion polls against the ruling Conservative Party.

Smith told Reuters in an interview that he saw transport as a key election issue. "I think it is a vote winner. People see chaos, mounting congestion and a fragmented transport network as a consequence of Tory neglect."
The existing regulatory regime for governing the newly privatised rail industry, in particular, was inadequate. The issue of Railtrack was foremost among his concerns.

"There is already a 700 million (pounds) backlog (of investment). Railtrack is a national monopoly and its investment is critical nationwide. We certainly won't be deflected by any delaying tactics which may be used by Railtrack," said Smith.

Smith said the maximum powers available were not being used to govern Railtrack which was privatised last May. "But the regulator can initiate a change to Railtrack's licence and can also seek to amend its track access conditions."
